applicableAreas: Southern property boundary along overhead electric line
findings.comment: Landscape plan shows proposed trees at 3.1 to 6 feet from overhead electric distribution conductor running along southern property boundary. Cedar Elm (non-utility-compatible per ECM Appendix F) and Live Oak (non-utility-compatible) specified on plant schedule are proposed as part of the mitigation trees. Trees must be repositioned to maintain minimum 15 lateral feet from outside conductor per UCM § 1.10.10.4, or species must be changed to utility-compatible alternatives.

applicableAreas: Southern property boundary along overhead electric line
findings.comment: Proposed large trees (Cedar Elm at 90 feet mature height, Live Oak at 60 feet mature height per ECM Appendix F) are located 3.1 to 6 feet from overhead electric distribution conductor. Large trees require minimum 25 lateral feet clearance from distribution conductors per UCM § 1.10.10.4. Trees must be repositioned or replaced with trees of compliant mature height (less than 40 feet).

Electrical utility poles are not clearly identified or labeled on the electrical design plan (Sheet 21) or landscape plan (Sheet 31). Proposed trees must maintain minimum 10 lateral feet from utility pole centerlines per UCM § 1.10.10.4, but this cannot be verified from submitted plans. Provide pole locations and identify all utility poles on the landscape plan with tree locations relative to poles clearly dimensioned or noted.

Electrical plan (Sheet 21) shows transformer pad locations (west of Buildings 2 and 8, east of Buildings 4 and 7), but landscape plan (Sheet 31) does not provide cross-reference or clear notation showing tree locations relative to transformer access doors. Trees must maintain 10 lateral feet from pad-mounted equipment access doors per UCM § 1.10.10.4. Provide dimension or cross-sheet reference showing tree clearances from transformer pads.

Electrical plan shows underground conduits and pull boxes routing through the site, but specific coordinates or dimensions for underground electrical equipment are not provided on the landscape plan. Trees must maintain minimum 5 lateral feet clearance from underground electrical equipment per UCM § 1.10.10.4. Provide detailed overlay or dimension showing tree locations relative to all underground electrical equipment with 5-foot clearances verified.

applicableAreas: Trees proposed within 20 feet of underground electrical equipment
findings.comment: Underground electrical equipment locations are not detailed on landscape plan, preventing verification of which trees fall within the 20-foot root barrier zone. Trees within 20 lateral feet of underground electric equipment require minimum 4-foot deep root barriers positioned 5 feet from equipment per UCM § 1.10.10.4. Provide detailed location plan showing underground equipment, 20-foot zones, tree locations, and root barrier specifications for any trees within affected zones.

applicableAreas: Southern property boundary near overhead electric line
findings.comment: Landscape plan (Sheet 31) shows proposed trees near overhead electric line but identifies them only by regulatory category symbols (M, SY, PL, P) with no species names. Plant schedule exists on Sheet 35 listing species, but landscape plan lacks cross-reference linking specific tree symbols to the species identified on the plant schedule. Proposed trees near utilities must be clearly identified by species directly on the landscape plan or through explicit cross-sheet notation.

applicableAreas: Southern property boundary near overhead electric line
findings.comment: Landscape plan does not differentiate large trees (mature height 40+ feet) from smaller trees near overhead electric facilities. Trees shown as 'M' symbols provide no indication of which are Cedar Elm (90 ft), Live Oak (60 ft), or smaller species (Mexican Redbud 20 ft, Texas Mountain Laurel 25 ft). Large tree species and mature heights must be clearly noted or indicated on the landscape plan to allow verification of clearance compliance.

Landscape plan does not show dimensioned clearances between proposed trees and overhead electric conductors. While field measurement identifies distances of 3.1 to 6 feet, plan dimensions and notes must clearly show that all clearances are measured from the outside conductor (not pole centerline) to the tree trunk center (not canopy edge) per UCM § 1.10.10.4 measurement methodology. Provide dimensions on landscape plan showing tree-to-conductor distances measured from proper reference points.

Landscape plan does not dimension clearances from tree trunks to overhead electric conductors. All clearance measurements must originate from tree trunk center (planting location symbol), not from projected canopy edge per UCM § 1.10.10.4. Provide dimension lines and notes on landscape plan confirming that clearances are measured from proper reference points.

applicableAreas: Southern property boundary along overhead electric line
findings.comment: Landscape plan proposes trees (Cedar Elm, Live Oak) within prohibited clearance zones (less than 15 feet from distribution conductors and less than 25 feet for large trees) without documented written approval from Austin Energy. Variations to standard tree placement distances and non-compatible species designations require explicit Austin Energy approval per UCM § 1.10.10.4. Provide signed approval letter from Austin Energy or revise landscape plan to maintain required clearances.
